fig1_polytropic_pv.svg: The same expansion of a gas from $V_1=0.1$ to $V_2=0.2$ m$^3$ starting at 3 bar, along three quasiequilibrium paths $pV^n=$ const (polytropic_pressure). The shaded area under each is the boundary work $W=\int p\,dV$ (polytropic_work): 30.0 kJ at constant pressure ($n=0$), 20.8 kJ isothermal ($n=1$), and 18.2 kJ for $n=1.4$. The larger $n$ is, the faster the pressure collapses as the gas expands, and the less work the same volume change delivers — the work depends on the PATH, not just on the end states.
fig2_energy_balance.svg: The closed-system first law $\Delta U=Q-W$, solved for the heat (heat_transfer) with $\Delta$KE and $\Delta$PE dropped. For a fixed internal-energy change each line has unit slope: every extra kilojoule of work the system delivers must be paid for by another kilojoule of heat in. The intercept is $\Delta U$ — an adiabatic process ($Q=0$) crosses the axis exactly where the work equals $-\Delta U$, i.e. the system does work only by spending its own internal energy.
